which_results_affected: Only Corollary cor:full-fk-range ("Combined finite-law parameter range", 00-introduction.tex:395–434), and only its 1<=q<4 case. That case is proved just by quoting the cited paper's main theorem (Thm 1.1(i) = intro:main(i), chordal SLE convergence), which is the result that fails. The paper's own main theorem (Theorem thm:main, 0<q<1, the result in the abstract) does not cite the failed paper anywhere, so the citation does not affect it. Nothing else references cor:full-fk-range.
evidence:
The paper cites the failed work exactly once (bib key OpenAI2026FKInterfacesAboveOne, references.bib:371–378). A grep of every .tex file finds no other \cite, \nocite or textual mention of it.

The one use is in sections/00-introduction.tex:421–434, in the proof of Corollary cor:full-fk-range ("fix $q\in(0,4)$ ... converges in law along the full mesh sequence to chordal $\SLE_{\kappa(q)}(D;a,b)$"):
"For $0<q<1$, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. For $1\le q<4$, let $W$ be the wired-arc boundary edges ... Thus the marginal on $E'$ is exactly the finite law used in \cite[Theorem~1.1(i)]{OpenAI2026FKInterfacesAboveOne}, which removes $W$ from sampling and declares its edges open for the same medial drawing. The wired/free arcs, orientation, marked approximation and curve metric agree, so that theorem proves the remaining range."

In the cited paper, Theorem 1.1(i) is intro:main(i) (sections/introduction.tex:194–201): "For every fixed real $1\le q<4$ ... the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in law ... to chordal $\SLE_{\kappa(q)}$". This is the main theorem that the Sec. 7.3 gap leaves unproved (via Thm hol:disk). The corollary's own argument is only a marginalization over the wired-arc edges, which is correct but does no work for this range. So the 1<=q<4 half of the corollary has no proof as written, and the claim for all of q in (0,4) falls back to (0,1).

Not affected: the abstract and Theorem thm:main cover only 0<q<1 ("For every fixed $0<q<1$, we prove ..."). The label cor:full-fk-range is never referenced anywhere else, and the organization paragraph and dependency figure route the main proof through the paper's own Sections 1–8. The other OpenAI citation (OpenAIConformalLimits2026, 07-observable.tex:220 and finite-calculus appendix:11) is a different paper. One caveat: the intro's framing at 00-introduction.tex:4 ("conjecture at the self-dual parameter for every fixed $0<q<4$") overstates what is proved if it presents the full range as settled. Also, the paper's own appendix (reflection-templates.tex:542) uses its own "norm diagrams" construction. That is not a citation, but since the method looks similar, its leaf-cost accounting may deserve a separate check against the same overcounting objection.
